newsitem.title: USA: Outboard drops dividend, to explore options.
newsitem.headline: Outboard drops dividend, to explore options.

text.p: Outboard Marine Corp said its board of directors elected not to declare a dividend this quarter and directed management to hire Salomon Brothers as its financial advisor to explore strategic alternatives for the company.

"The company's board of directors believes the capital base of the company must be strengthened in order to allow it to accelerate the operational and strategic changes under way at OMC, and to fund a more rapid development of the company's FICHT fuel injection technology and other product development initiatives," the company said.

Outboard reported a fiscal second-quarter net loss of $7.3 million, versus a year-ago quarterly profit of $1.1 million. Sales on the quarter were down to $237 million from $285.5 million in the same period ended March 31 a year ago.

"OMC's sales decrease was due primarily to reduced market demand, both domestically and internationally, coupled with a managed effort to assist dealers in reducing field inventories," said chief executive Harry Bowman.
On a year-to-year basis, dealer inventories of OMC outboard engines were down about 16 percent, while boat inventories were down about one percent, the company said.
"Retail consumer programs were very successful in the field inventory reduction effort, although they resulted in higher sales discounts for the quarter," Bowman said.

The earnings decline was primarily a result of the lower sales, Outboard said. Another cause was "unabsorbed manufacturing expenses arising from reduced production schedules as well as costs associated with the company's earnings improvement program," it said.
Earnings were also hit by increased marketing expenses related to intorduction of the company's new FICHT fuel injection engines, Outboard said.
